---
title: "IBI36 Copernicus Marine reference"
---

The IBI36 reader opens the regional multiyear physical reference from
[Copernicus Marine product IBI_MULTIYEAR_PHY_005_002](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/IBI_MULTIYEAR_PHY_005_002),
at its native 1/36 degree resolution. It uses the same Copernicus Marine Toolbox
as the GLORYS and GLO12 readers and returns standard OceanBench variables.

## Open a small subset

Use an existing OceanBench environment and Copernicus Marine account. The Toolbox
uses its configured credentials when `username` and `password` are omitted; it
may prompt if needed. Keep passwords out of source code and notebooks.

```python
from oceanbench.datasets.reference import ibi36_reference

with ibi36_reference(
    "2023-12-11",
    "2023-12-11",
    minimum_longitude=-10,
    maximum_longitude=-9.85,
    minimum_latitude=43,
    maximum_latitude=43.15,
    maximum_depth=10,
) as reference:
    subset = reference.isel(
        time=0, latitude=slice(0, 5), longitude=slice(0, 5)
    )
    print(subset)
```

Dates are inclusive. Spatial and positive-down depth limits restrict the remote
subset. Source timestamps are at midnight UTC and are preserved. Selecting and
printing this subset does not compute its ocean fields or save a dataset.
Use the context manager, or call `reference.close()`, to close all opened sources.

## Sources, variables and mask

The reader pins dataset version `202511` and opens these daily datasets:

| Dataset ID | Native variable | OceanBench variable | Units |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cmems_mod_ibi_phy-temp_my_0.027deg_P1D-m` | `thetao` | `sea_water_potential_temperature` | `degrees_C` |
| `cmems_mod_ibi_phy-sal_my_0.027deg_P1D-m` | `so` | `sea_water_salinity` | `1e-3` |
| `cmems_mod_ibi_phy-cur_my_0.027deg_P1D-m` | `uo` | `eastward_sea_water_velocity` | `m/s` |
| `cmems_mod_ibi_phy-cur_my_0.027deg_P1D-m` | `vo` | `northward_sea_water_velocity` | `m/s` |
| `cmems_mod_ibi_phy-ssh_my_0.027deg_P1D-m` | `zos` | `sea_surface_height_above_geoid` | `m` |

Practical salinity values are retained without division by 1000. Daily mean
currents are already oriented eastward and northward; no vector rotation or
de-tiding is applied. Their signs and values in metres per second are retained.
The output uses `time`, `depth`, `latitude` and
`longitude`; the Toolbox supplies positive-down depth in metres, rather than
the underlying negative elevation coordinate.

A fifth source supplies the native static ocean mask:
`cmems_mod_ibi_phy_my_0.027deg-3D_static`, part `bathy`, variable `mask`, at the
same dataset version. Its horizontal subset matches the data subset.

The mask is read from the surface through the deepest selected source level.
Temperature, salinity and currents use the matching depth levels, masking land and cells
below the bottom. Sea-surface height always uses the surface ocean mask, even
when only deep temperature and salinity levels are requested. A missing or
incompatible mask raises an error instead of returning unmasked fields.

## Interpolate to an existing grid

Use the actual coordinates of an already-open target dataset, for example a
challenger on a 1/12 degree grid. A spacing alone does not identify that grid:
its cell centres must also match. Open the reference over the target domain,
including surrounding source cells needed by linear interpolation.

The following assumes that `target_grid` is already open and lies inside the
small reference domain shown above:

```python
from oceanbench.core.interpolate import interpolate_to_grid

with ibi36_reference(
    "2023-12-11",
    "2023-12-11",
    minimum_longitude=-10,
    maximum_longitude=-9.85,
    minimum_latitude=43,
    maximum_latitude=43.15,
    maximum_depth=10,
) as reference:
    reference_on_target = interpolate_to_grid(reference, target_grid)
```

This shared helper preserves the target latitude and longitude coordinates
exactly. It does not extrapolate outside the source domain or invent a regular
1/12 degree grid. Ocean fields remain lazy and retain missing masked values.
Keep the reference open while computing any derived result.

`interpolate_1_degree` keeps its existing 1 degree behaviour for every reference,
including IBI36. Neither example performs a model evaluation or monthly extraction.
